"Quiet fortnight policy on spare blankets"
The aim of this section is to explain what applies on every shift

Companion Animal Travel Desk Standards for Animal Handling

This section sets out the routine checks and respectful service expected at Aurelia Skyways when a passenger books or presents an animal for travel. Staff should use calm, plain language, verify the booking details carefully, and keep the passenger informed about any welfare step that affects the journey. The desk welcomes questions in a warm professional tone, and the record should always show that the animal was reviewed with care.

The welfare coordinator reviews comfort needs before acceptance, including crate condition, ventilation, feeding arrangements, and any reasonable support that can be offered without weakening safety. Staff should look for signs that the crate is secure, clean, and suitable for the species involved, and they should escalate any concern rather than guess. When a passenger arrives worried, the response must be steady and helpful, with the facts checked against the booking notes and the guidance held by the desk. <<FACT F064>> The passenger should then be told what action will follow and why, in clear terms that avoid pressure or blame.

For larger animals, the acceptance review is more detailed because handling, rest, and loading may need extra attention. <<FACT F075>> If a case does not meet the stated requirement, staff must explain the result without argument, offer the next lawful option where one exists, and document the reason in the file. Cabin team staff are expected to monitor animals during flight and report any issue at once so that the desk can support a safe response. Supervisors should listen carefully when a passenger is distressed, confirm the facts, and help the team keep the exchange orderly and respectful.

Any uncertainty about acceptance, welfare, or post-booking changes must be referred without delay to the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at Companion Animal Travel Desk.
